items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: He's a nephew, that's his nephew. ... Abby's seen him here. ... I guess Abby won't take any sugar, huh? Nothing.

ctx.x: He looks like that fella that booked us across the river one time. He's a, I believe he's a cousin, he's a cousin of Abby, you know him? He's a nephew, that's his nephew. Well this fella booked me across the river about three years ago. Well that's Abby's nephew. And he just recently died? No, no, his daddy. He's daddy. His daddy was in a wheelchair. Yeah. His daddy came to hear us that afternoon. We played over in Gretna.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: he sends Abby Brunus in each place to play that carnival parade... he kept on playing until... with me... when he sent little Brunus in his place

ctx.x: Yes. And, uh, of course, it happened to be close to a Mardi Gras. And I had three bands out that year. And, uh, well, little Brunus, Abby, he was a pretty fair corner player. It was then at that time, too. He was picking up mighty nice, very nice. Well, he sends Abby Brunus in each place to play that carnival parade. While he went around scouting, I guess, to get members to go north with, see? Now, he claims he went first there, to went up north first. No. I believe Tom Brown was a man who went up north first. I…
I believe he went a year before or so.
